$comment: The $id stays pinned to the v2.0.0 path — but as of v2.4.0 the REASON has changed, and the old reason is no longer true. It used to read 'the structural schema is unchanged across 2.0.0–2.3.0': every release through 2.3.0 (including the LIP-0008 A-5 relaxation) was validator-level, so this file was byte-stable. v2.4.0 (LIP-0010 Option D) is the FIRST structural change — it adds two optional enum properties, `authority` and `production`, under $defs.reserved, and BACK-FILLS `interaction`, which has been validated by canvas_std since v2.2.0 but was never recorded in this properties list (F-GL-1: three hand-maintained copies of one namespace, none of them read). The $id is retained because the change is purely ADDITIVE and $defs.reserved sets no additionalProperties:false, so every document valid under the 2.0.0–2.3.0 schema remains valid here: the canonical URL keeps its promise. Semantic and version-specific rules still live in the canvas_std validator, not in this JSON Schema — the A-8 co-requirement ('two keys or neither') is a validator rule, because JSON Schema cannot express it without a dependentRequired pair that would also have to be kept in sync by hand.
title: aDNA Canvas Standard v2.4.0
description: Structural contract for a .canvas document. Node/edge floor + enums + the _reserved carrier. Semantic checks (toEnd:arrow / C-4, id resolution, sequence-acyclicity, exactly-one-canonical-surface, the A-8 authority/production co-requirement) are performed by the canvas_std validator (validate / validate_suite) — JSON Schema cannot express them.

reserved.description: aDNA-native extensions (aDNA-Native level). Stripping this block yields a valid baseline canvas (C4 degradation).
